title: Pre-deployment Authorization Failure Modes and Forensic Checklist
author: Aisha Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook documents anticipated authorization (RBAC/authz) failure modes that can occur during or immediately after pre-deployment and provides a forensic preservation and evidence-collection checklist to meet regulatory and internal compliance expectations. It is intended for security engineers, SREs, release approvers, and incident responders who must preserve evidentiary artifacts for audits, legal holds, or cross-region incident investigations.

Scope

- Applicable to: all model-serving, control-plane, and customer-metadata services that are staged or deployed through Redwood CI/CD pipelines.
- NOT applicable to purely client-side UI features (see UI release checklist).
- Regions: global; data-residency notes are included per-customer region.

Owner and escalation

- Primary owner: Security Response (security oncall rota).
- Secondary owner: Platform SRE oncall.
- Pager duties: security@redwood (primary), platform-oncall@redwood (secondary).

Summary of common pre-deployment authorization failure modes

1) Policy Drift at Compile-time
- Cause: Policy-as-code (OPA/Rego) changes not included in the same PR as code requiring new entitlements.
- Symptom: Deployment passes CI but runtime denies new API verbs for service identity -> 403s in smoke tests.

2) Attribute Broker Mapping Mismatch
- Cause: Identity provider (IDP) attribute changes (groups/claims) vs. attribute-to-role mapping in attribute broker.
- Symptom: Users with expected roles lose access; automated canary requests show permission errors.

3) JIT Provisioning Race
- Cause: Just-in-time entitlement activation (JIT) race between provisioning pipeline and service startup.
- Symptom: Temporary 401/403 windows for new instances during scale-up.

4) Service Identity Rotation/Key Mismatch
- Cause: Missing secret rotation step or stale service account token in image.
- Symptom: Mutual TLS/Tokens rejected; inter-service auth fails during deployment.

5) Environment-scoped Policy Leak
- Cause: Dev policy accidentally applied in stage/prod through IaC misconfig.
- Symptom: Over-permissive access in target environment or missing constraints.

Audit and logging prerequisites (what to capture and where)

- Minimum required event set (all services):
  - authn:login_attempt, authn:token_issue, authn:token_refresh
  - authz:policy_evaluation (include decision, policy_id, input_hash)
  - authz:decision_denied (include resource, principal, action, reason_id)
  - identity:attribute_change (old_claims, new_claims, actor, source_commit)
  - service:identity_rotation (service_id, old_key_id, new_key_id, rotate_actor)
  - pipeline:deploy_action (ci_job_id, commit_sha, artifact_id, target_namespace)

- Schema fields (required per event): timestamp, event_id, service, environment, region, request_id/correlation_id, principal_id, resource, action, outcome, policy_version, raw_payload_link.

- Retention and SLOs:
  - Ingest SLO: 99.9% of auth events available in audit index within 60 seconds of occurrence.
  - Retention baseline: 365 days hot; 5 years cold (for enterprise customers with contract).
  - Evidence hold policy: When a legal hold is opened, retention escalates to immutable 7-year hold for related objects.

Pre-deployment gating and SDLC checks (automated and manual)

Automated gates (must pass):
1) Policy-as-code test suite (unit + integration): no new deny decisions for baseline smoke requests.
   - Command example: 
     opa test -v policy/
2) Attribute mapping CI: compare IDP claim fixture to mapping table; fail on unmapped required attributes.
3) Authz simulation: run canary simulator against staging with new policy bundle.
   - Example: ./tools/authz-sim --bundle build/policy.tar.gz --test-suite smoke.json
4) Secret scaffolding validation: verify rotated credentials baked into image manifest.
   - Terraform plan checks and baked-in envscan: tfsec + internal secret-scanner.

Manual gates (required if any automated gate fails or high blast radius):
- Security review signoff in PR (security reviewer must check RBAC diffs).
- Scoped deployment windows for cross-region changes.

Detection and immediate containment steps (runbook)

1) Detect
- Alert triggers: sudden spike in authz:decision_denied for a service (>500/min for 5m) or failed smoke test post-deploy.
- Query example: authz_decisions | where service=="model-router" and outcome=="deny" | count_over_time(5m).

2) Contain
- If high-volume denies causing outage: roll back the deployment to previous artifact_id with known-good policy bindings.
- If isolated to single namespace, temporarily disable new policy bundle (use emergency-allow only with strict audit).

3) Preserve Evidence (first 2 hours are critical)
- Snapshot audit index segment containing relevant request_ids.
- Collect the following artifacts (minimum):
  - CI artifact manifest (ci_job_id, commit_sha)
  - Policy bundle (policy tarball) and policy bundle hash
  - Attribute broker mapping file at deployment time
  - IDP audit for attribute changes (export for time window +/- 1 hour)
  - Service logs (stdout/stderr), structured auth logs, and runtime metrics for the affected instances
  - Kubernetes API server audit logs for the target namespace (if applicable)
  - Machine images/tarball or container image digest for deployed artifacts
  - KMS key rotation logs and secret manager access logs for rotation window
  - Network flow logs (VPC flow / equivalent) if lateral movement suspected

- For each artifact include: collector name, start/end time, and storage location (immutable).
- Use evidence packaging tool: ./bin/evidence-collector --case-id <INCID> --artifact <type> --out s3://evidence-bucket/<INCID>/

Preservation commands / examples

- Elastic snapshot: curl -XPUT "${ES_HOST}/_snapshot/evidence_repo/snap-<INCID>?wait_for_completion=true" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"indices":"auth-*", "ignore_unavailable":true}'
- Kubernetes API audit slice: kubectl logs -n kube-system audit-logger --since=2h | gzip > /tmp/<INCID>-k8s-audit.gz
- IDP export (example for Okta via API): curl -s -H "Authorization: SSWS $OKTA_TOKEN" "https://api.okta.com/v1/logs?since=2026-01-12T00:00:00Z" > /tmp/<INCID>-okta-logs.json

Data residency and retention considerations

- If the incident involves customer data from region-bound customers (EU, UK, APAC), evidence copies must be stored in the same geo-fence for the duration of legal/local privacy holds. See: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/geo-smart-retention-and-audit-evidence-playbook-2027 for mapping rules.
- When transferring evidence for cross-border legal requests, consult Legal and Data Privacy before moving copies across regions.

Evidentiary packaging and chain-of-custody

- Evidence package metadata (required fields): case_id, collected_by, collected_at (UTC), artifact_type, original_location, integrity_hash (SHA256), storage_location, custody_chain (list of principal_ids), legal_hold_flag.
- Signing: all packaged artifacts must be signed by collector via internal signing service (signer-service).
- Maintain immutable audit trail for all access to evidence bucket; access requires two-person approval for restricted cases.

Compliance evidence workflow (timeline and responsibilities)

- T+0–2h: detection, containment, and initial evidence snapshot (security & platform).
- T+2–24h: complete evidence collection and package creation (assigned forensics engineer).
- T+24–72h: preliminary incident brief and evidence submission to Legal & Compliance (security).
- T+72h+: deep investigation, timeline reconstruction, and executive summary (security + SRE + Product).

Requesting and approving risk exceptions (pre-deploy)

- If a deployment requires an authorization exception (e.g., temporary broad role for migration), submit an authorization-exception request via the risk registry with the following:
  - business rationale, duration, compensating controls (audit sampling cadence, additional monitoring), rollback plan, and list of impacted principals.
- Approval requires: Security lead + Platform lead signoff. Exceptions >72h require Legal review.

Post-incident controls and SDLC hardening recommendations

- Enforce policy-as-code bundles are always reviewed in the same PR as application changes.
- Expand authz simulation coverage to include negative and race-condition scenarios.
- Add CI check: alert on any PR that modifies attribute mapping files without Security reviewer.
- Automate evidence packaging for any pre-deploy smoke test failure to reduce time-to-preservation.

Diagnostics and useful queries (examples)

- Find all denies for a principal in a time window:
  authz_decisions | where principal_id==":principal" and outcome=="deny" | sort timestamp desc
- Link CI job to deny events: join authz_decisions on correlation_id == ci.correlation_id where ci.commit_sha=="<sha>"

Appendix: quick checklist (for responders)

1) Identify scope (services, namespaces, customers)
2) Trigger containment (rollback or disable new policy bundle)
3) Snapshot audit index and export IDP logs
4) Collect policy bundle, attribute mapping, and CI artifact manifests
5) Package artifacts, compute SHA256, sign package, and place in evidence-bucket
6) Notify Legal if customer data or cross-border flows are involved
7) Open risk-exception entry if temporary mitigations are applied
